summary: Sets the locale every IonBase component reads: react-aria's provider, re-exported. For right-to-left it is half the switch — arrow keys follow the locale, while the layout follows `dir` on the page.
useWhen: the app is in a language other than the browser's, or must not depend on it
the app is right-to-left: an RTL locale here, and `dir="rtl"` on the root element

useInstead.when: one region should be in the other theme
useInstead.why: a locale is language and direction; a theme is colour

composition.note: Mount it once, around the whole app, with the locale the product is written in (`he-IL`, `ar-EG`, `en-GB`). With no `locale`, react-aria falls back to the browser's language. It decides the arrow keys in Tabs, Toolbar, Menu, TreeView, Slider and the calendars, the order of date segments, and number formatting; it does not set `dir`. Right-to-left is both: `dir="rtl"` on <html> for the layout — every stylesheet is logical, so nothing else is needed — and an RTL locale here for the keys. Set only one and the page is mirrored but ← still moves back, or the keys flip on a page that is not mirrored.

guarantees: with an RTL locale, arrow keys move in the reading direction: ← goes forward along a toolbar, a tab list or a slider
react-aria's own strings — a calendar's Previous and Next, a date field's segment names — are announced in the locale's language
requires: `dir` on the root element to match the locale's direction, and `lang` to match the content's language
notes: `useLocale()` is re-exported with it and returns `{ locale, direction }`, for a component of the app's own that has to know.

antiPatterns.why: the page mirrors, but react-aria's arrow keys still move as if left-to-right: → steps back through a toolbar that now reads right to left

antiPatterns.dont: one provider per component or per page
antiPatterns.why: the locale is the app's; nested providers let parts of a page disagree about the language and the direction
